chapter.title: Meet the builder: the terminal and your first request

cards.body: You've hired a builder, and the *terminal* is the driveway where you meet them: a plain text window where you type instead of click. Picture a black screen with one blinking cursor, like an empty lot with a single flag in the ground. **Whichever folder you're standing in when you say "start" is the house the builder works on.**
cards.simpler: The terminal is a plain window where you type words instead of clicking buttons. It looks like a black screen with one blinking line. Think of it as the driveway where you meet a builder you've hired. You stand in a folder, then tell the builder to start. **Whichever folder you're standing in when you say "start" is the house the builder works on.** So pick your spot first.

cards.prompt: You open the terminal, step into a folder on your Desktop called pet-rock-fanpage, and start Claude Code. You ask for a web page. Where does the new file land?

options.text: Inside pet-rock-fanpage, the folder you were standing in
In Downloads, like everything else on this computer
Somewhere hidden that only Claude can see

whyNot.b: That's where browsers drop files, not where the builder works: Claude Code builds in the folder you opened it from.
whyNot.c: That's a worry, not how it works: every file Claude makes is an ordinary file you can open and see.

cards.reteach: The builder only works on the house you walked them into. Start Claude Code inside a folder, and that folder is where every file appears. Change folders, and you've changed houses.

cards.title: Open the driveway
cards.body:
On a Mac the terminal app is called Terminal. Open it and you'll see a short line of text and a cursor. It's waiting for you to type.

First make a *folder*, also called a directory, for the project. Then step into it with the command `cd`, which means change directory. For a folder named hello-site on your Desktop you'd type `cd Desktop/hello-site` and press Enter.

Install Claude Code once with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`. After that, **typing `claude` inside a folder starts the builder in that folder.** You'll see a prompt where you can type plain English.
cards.simpler:
On a Mac the terminal app is called Terminal. Open it. You'll see a short line of text and a blinking cursor waiting for you.

Make a folder for your project. Then step into it by typing `cd` and the folder name. For a folder called hello-site on your Desktop, type `cd Desktop/hello-site` and press Enter.

Install Claude Code once with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`. After that, **typing `claude` inside a folder starts the builder in that folder.** Then you can type in plain English.

cards.title: Maya's green hello
cards.body:
Maya makes an empty folder called hello-site on her Desktop. In Terminal she types `cd Desktop/hello-site`, then `claude`. She writes: "Make one web page that says Hello from Maya in big green letters, and open it in my browser."

Claude asks if it may create a file called index.html. She presses Enter to say yes. Her browser opens. The letters are green, which is somehow the most surprising part.
cards.simpler:
Maya makes an empty folder called hello-site on her Desktop. In Terminal she types `cd Desktop/hello-site`, then `claude`. She writes: "Make one web page that says Hello from Maya in big green letters, and open it in my browser."

Claude asks if it can make a file called index.html. She presses Enter to say yes. Her browser opens. **The letters are green**, which is somehow the most surprising part.

cards.prompt: Jonas opens Terminal and types `claude` right away, without stepping into any folder. He's in his home folder, the big one that holds Documents, Pictures, everything. Then he asks for a to-do page. What's the catch?

options.text: Claude can't make files from there, so nothing happens
It works, but the builder is now standing in his whole house; the file lands among all his stuff, so he should make a project folder first
He has to type `claude` a second time to confirm

whyNot.a: That's the permission step, not a dead end: Claude can build anywhere you start it, which is exactly the problem here.
whyNot.c: That's the yes-or-no permission prompt, not a repeat command: you type `claude` once and answer its questions after.

cards.reteach: Where you stand is where the builder works. Starting in your home folder means every new file mixes with your personal files. One empty folder per project keeps each house separate.

cards.title: Say yes, then look
cards.body:
Before Claude creates or runs anything, it asks. You'll see a question like "Create index.html?" with a yes option. Press Enter or type y. This is the builder checking with you before cutting a hole in the wall.

Then comes the part most people skip. **Look at the result with your own eyes.** Open the folder and find the new file. If the page opened in your browser, read what's on it.

If you can't point at the thing and say "that's what I asked for," the job isn't done yet. When you're finished for the day, type `/exit` to leave.
cards.simpler:
Before Claude makes or runs anything, it asks you first. You'll see a question like "Create index.html?" Press Enter or type y to say yes. It's like a builder checking before cutting into a wall.

Then comes the step most people skip. **Look at the result with your own eyes.** Open the folder and find the new file. If a page opened in your browser, read it.

If you can't point at it and say "that's what I asked for," it isn't done. When you're finished, type `/exit`.

cards.body: Priya's first ever request is "Build me a budgeting app with login, charts and dark mode." Twenty minutes later there are 14 files and nothing she can open and check. She can't tell if it worked, so she can't tell what to fix. *Spot it:* if your first request can't be judged in one glance at the screen, it's too big for day one. Ask for one page you can see.
cards.simpler: Priya's very first request is "Build me a budgeting app with login, charts and dark mode." Twenty minutes later there are 14 files and nothing she can open and check. She can't tell if it worked, so she can't tell what to fix. **If your first request can't be judged in one glance at the screen, it's too big for day one.** Ask for one page you can see instead.

cards.prompt: Your friend texts: "Claude Code said it made the file, but there's nothing there." What's the most likely reason?

options.text: They started Claude Code in one folder and are looking in a different one
Claude Code only works with the internet switched off
They typed the request in capital letters

whyNot.b: That's backwards: Claude Code needs the internet to talk to Claude, and that has nothing to do with where files land.
whyNot.c: That's a style choice, not a rule: Claude reads plain English in any case, and the file still lands in the folder you started from.

cards.reteach: The file is always in the folder Claude Code was started from. Ask your friend which folder they typed `claude` in, and look there. The builder never leaves the house you walked them into.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: The terminal is a text window; step into an empty folder with `cd`, type `claude`, and that folder is where the builder works. **Ask for one small thing you can see, say yes when it asks, then look at the result yourself.**
cards.simpler: The terminal is a text window. Step into an empty folder with `cd`, type `claude`, and that folder is where the builder works. **Ask for one small thing you can see, say yes when it asks, then look at the result yourself.** That's the whole loop. Small request, quick yes, then check with your own eyes before asking for more.

cards.body: Tonight: make an empty folder on your Desktop, open Terminal, type `cd Desktop/your-folder`, then `claude`. Ask for one page with your name on it, opened in your browser. Then go find the file.
cards.simpler: Tonight, try it for real. Make an empty folder on your Desktop. Open Terminal and type `cd Desktop/your-folder`, then type `claude`. Ask for one page with your name on it, opened in your browser. Say yes when it asks. **Then go find the file yourself** and look at it. That one small page is the whole point of day one.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now start Claude Code in a folder, type a plain-English request, and see a file appear and run.
